candidates.change_summary: Delete the require statement, so a failed sub-call no longer reverts and forward completes silently even on failure.
Replace callee with msg.sender so the call target becomes the caller instead of the provided address.
Replace callee with address(this) so the contract calls itself instead of the given target.
Delete the _data argument and replace with empty bytes so the call always sends empty calldata regardless of input.
Changed the success requirement from require(_s) to assert(_s); this introduces a Panic(0x01) revert instead of a plain Error when the external call fails.
Changed the success requirement to accept failed external calls by requiring !_s instead of _s, causing opposite revert behavior for failed and successful calls.
Replace the required successful call result with its negation, making forward revert exactly when callee.call succeeds and complete when it fails.
Remove the success check so the low-level call result is no longer required to be true.
Replace the low-level call with a successful no-op, so forward no longer makes the external call.
Replace the require on the low-level call success flag with a require that it failed, making forward revert exactly when the callee call succeeds.
Ignore the low-level call success flag by requiring a constant true, so forward completes even when the callee call fails and bubbles no revert.
Replace the call success check so that a failed callee call causes forward to complete instead of revert.
Delete the require statement checking the callee call success, so a failed callee call does not revert forward.
Remove the require(_s) assertion so forward no longer reverts when the callee call fails.
Change the callee call to a staticcall, causing forward to revert on state-changing callees.
Replace the propagated call success with a hardcoded true requirement, removing the revert-on-failed-call behavior.
Delete the require statement so a failed external call no longer causes forward to revert.
Delete the require(_s) check after the external call, so a failed callee call no longer reverts forward.
Replace require(_s) with require(!_s), reverting when the callee call succeeds and completing when it fails.
